groups.note: County, municipal, school, and special-district names are keyed from official Platte clerk general summaries (2020, 2022, 2024, and 2026; official 2026 names and totals were read from official rendered page images because the official PDF text is font-encoded), the official May 6, 2025 Hartville municipal canvass, and the official Town of Glendo government page retrieved from the Wayback Machine (captures 2024-02-21 and 2026-07-08) because the live official town site returned 500/406. Official 2014–2018 Platte clerk general canvasses were not found on the live clerk URL patterns, and a Wayback CDX search of media/Elections/* for 2014–2019 returned no captures, so January 2015–2020 county, municipal, school, and special-district rows are largely Not yet collected rather than invented. Multi-county legislative seats use official SOS district-wide Total rows, with the official Platte share noted, for every keyed year (2012 and 2016–2020 S02; 2024 and 2026 S06; 2014–2026 H04). Official SOS two-column pages were cut at the next district header. After 2022 redistricting, official SOS S02 is Converse and Natrona only; official Platte S02 is ended at January 2023 rather than inventing a holdover, so January 2023–2024 Platte senate coverage is Not yet collected. Official S06 begins after the official 2024 election. Official 2016–2020 SOS S06 Platte rows are blank (Laramie-only on the pre-2022 map) and are not copied as Platte terms. Official Goshen slivers for Platte County School District #1 and #2 are combined into the official whole-district result in 2020 (PCSD #1 only), 2022, 2024, and 2026; ranking did not change. No official 2020 Goshen sliver for PCSD #2 was found. Write-in-only official contests with no named certified winner are not seated. The official 2025 Hartville canvass has no mayor contest, so the Hartville mayor stays Not yet collected. Official July 8, 2026 Glendo page still lists 2026-ending officers and is not treated as a post-May 2026 current roster; current Glendo mayor and council stay Not yet collected. Chugwater cemetery and fire rows use official Platte totals; official Goshen slivers for those contests were not combined here.

groups.note: Supreme Court justices and the Chancery Court judge are the people in office this January, from official Wyoming Judicial Branch dates and official retention results (shared with other counties). Official 2026 Platte clerk retentions for Justice Bridget Hill (YES 2,330, NO 745), Justice Robert C. Jarosh (YES 2,211, NO 742), and Chancery Court Judge Ben Burningham (YES 2,329, NO 690) are those statewide retentions, not local 8th JD seats. Local rows are 8th Judicial District judges (Converse, Goshen, Niobrara, and Platte). Full names are taken from official Wyoming Judicial Branch 8th JD court pages and official Platte clerk retention lines, and those sources are cited. Official 2022 Platte clerk prints 'EIGHTH JUDICIAL DIST CIRCUIT COURT JUDGE ALL' (YES 2,920, NO 643); that official heading is truncated on the official page and is not used to invent the retained judge's name. Judges of other districts are not copied here.
